opportunities.title: Small grants

amount.raw: Awards vary according to project but will only exceptionally exceed £6,000 and will generally fall in a range of £1,500-£5,000. Travel/subsistence in Japan up to £2,000 per person for trips up to 13 days, up to £2,500 per person for 14+ days. Up to £5,000 for PhD fieldwork visits of six months or more. Japan office up to ¥300,000 for PhD students travelling to the UK.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants must belong to, or provide evidence of support from, an organisation or institution willing to receive grant funds. Applications are not accepted from individuals seeking support for personal projects. Welcomes applications from any field including arts and culture, humanities and social issues, Japanese language, medicine and health, science, youth and education, and sport.
opportunities.summary: Seed funding to enable UK-Japan projects that might otherwise not be possible, bringing people in the UK and Japan together to deepen mutual understanding, exchange ideas or expertise, or develop lasting collaboration. Supports festivals, workshops, performances, exchanges, collaborative projects, Japanese language teaching, and academic research/visits.

opportunities.title: Butterfield Awards in Medicine and Health

deadlines.raw: 1 December (decision in March of the following year)

amount.raw: Butterfield Awards of up to £10,000; continuing projects lasting up to three years to a maximum of £10,000 per year, to a total limit of £30,000.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants should normally be able to show an existing research record, but consideration is also given to practitioners, managers, carers or others in health-related fields. Project must involve partners in both the UK and Japan. Preference given to those not previously involved in UK-Japan collaboration and early-career applicants.
opportunities.summary: Supports exchanges and collaborations between health and medical professionals in Japan and the UK, including study of scientific, clinical, social and economic issues in healthcare, creating opportunities for researchers, practitioners, policy makers, managers and voluntary sector workers to share knowledge and develop new approaches. Grants may be used for travel, conference and publication costs.
